effects.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
effects.original_authors: Liu, C; Kelnar, K; Liu, B; Chen, X; Calhoun-Davis, T; Li, H; Patrawala, L; Yan, H; Jeter, C; Honorio, S; Wiggins, J; Bader, A; Fagin, R; Brown, D; Tang, D
effects.replication_study: Expression of miR-34a in LAPC4 cells (Figure 1; original Figure 1B; Registered Report Protocol 3)
effects.outcome: miR-34a expression (qRT-PCR, normalized to miR-103) in FACS-sorted CD44+ vs CD44- LAPC4 cells purified from xenograft tumors
effects.timepoint: not applicable: single cross-sectional measurement after sorting
effects.description: miR-34a is underexpressed in CD44+ prostate cancer stem-like LAPC4 cells relative to CD44- cells (reported at 3.4% of the CD44- level).
effects.citation_sentence: We independently replicated an experiment to determine miR-34a expression in CD44[+] and CD44[-] LAPC4 cells. This experiment is comparable to what was reported in Figure 1B of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 3 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
effects.evidence: Results, 'Expression of miR-34a in LAPC4 cells' / Figure 1: "miR-34a was elevated in level in CD44[+] cells, being expressed at 202% of the level in the CD44[-] cells" ... "To summarize, for this experiment we found results that were in the same direction as the original study for let-7b expression, but not for miR-34a expression."
effects.notes: Direction opposite to original (202% vs 3.4%), but one biological repeat and no inferential test, so not coded reversal (no significance; authors say only 'not in the same direction'). Authors flag a confound: CD44 staining was weak/indistinguishable from isotype control, so CD44+ was redefined as top 1% (original/RR: top 10%), and the CD44- group may contain CD44+ cells; a second coder could call this inconclusive. let-7b (also underexpressed in the original, reduced here 'as expected') is treated as a reference/control comparison, not a separate claim; a coder who treats it as a claim would add a success row. Replication type: authors call the whole effort 'This direct replication'; gating change and different LAPC4 source are deviations (close experiment is a plausible alternative).

effects.original_authors: Liu, C; Kelnar, K; Liu, B; Chen, X; Calhoun-Davis, T; Li, H; Patrawala, L; Yan, H; Jeter, C; Honorio, S; Wiggins, J; Bader, A; Fagin, R; Brown, D; Tang, D
effects.replication_study: Effect of miR-34a expression on tumor growth (Figure 2B,C; original Supplemental Figure 5C; Registered Report Protocol 4)
effects.outcome: Weight of xenograft tumors (also tumor volume over time) from lentivirally miR-34a-transduced LAPC4 cells in male NOD/SCID mice
effects.contrast: miR-34a-transduced vs negative-control (scramble) transduced LAPC4 cells
effects.timepoint: end of experiment when control tumors reached ~0.54 g (100 days post injection in replication; 69 days in original)
effects.description: Enforced lentiviral expression of miR-34a in purified LAPC4 cells inhibits tumor regeneration in NOD/SCID mice (smaller tumors than negative-control-transduced cells).
effects.citation_sentence: LAPC4 tumor cells were used to replicate an experiment that tested the effect of miR-34a on tumor growth. This experiment is similar to what was reported in Supplemental Figure 5C of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 4 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
effects.evidence: Results, 'Effect of miR-34a expression on tumor growth' / Figure 2B: miR-34a 0.55 g vs control 0.51 g; "The planned comparisons of the miR-34a group to the negative control group (t(18) = 0.432, p=0.671) ... were not statistically significant." "To summarize, we found results that were not in the same direction as the original study and not statistically significant." Meta-analysis (Figure 4A): opposite direction, p=0.510.
effects.notes: Authors' summary is a failure statement. Caveat: miR-34a was undetectable in the excised tumors (silenced in vivo), and authors note 'this observation does not necessarily imply miR-34a does not suppress tumor growth ... since miR-34a overexpression was not confirmed in vivo' -- a coder might code inconclusive on validity grounds. Point estimate slightly opposite, non-significant: not reversal. Untransduced group added as extra control (no row). Different LAPC4 source and 48 h vs 24 h infection-to-injection are deviations; same lentiviral vectors, cell line and strain, and authors call it a direct replication.

effects.original_title: The microRNA miR-34a inhibits prostate cancer stem cells and metastasis by directly repressing CD44
effects.original_authors: Liu, C; Kelnar, K; Liu, B; Chen, X; Calhoun-Davis, T; Li, H; Patrawala, L; Yan, H; Jeter, C; Honorio, S; Wiggins, J; Bader, A; Fagin, R; Brown, D; Tang, D
effects.replication_study: CD44 Western blot in excised tumors (Figure 2E; original Figure 4A; Registered Report Protocol 5)
effects.outcome: CD44 protein expression (Western blot, normalized to beta-actin) in xenograft tumors
effects.contrast: tumors from miR-34a-transduced vs control (negative-control-transduced / untransduced) cells
effects.timepoint: not applicable: measured once in excised tumors at end of tumor experiment
effects.description: In tumors formed from miR-34a-transduced prostate cancer cells (DU145, retroviral vector), CD44 expression is reduced, inversely correlating with miR-34a expression.
effects.citation_sentence: This experiment was described in Protocol 5 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015) and is conceptually similar to what was reported in Figure 4A of Liu et al. (2011), which used DU145 cells transduced with a retroviral vector encoding miR-34a.
effects.evidence: Results / Figure 2E: "we found CD44 expression in tumors derived from miR-34a transduced LAPC4 cells was similar to the expression in tumors derived from untransduced or negative control transduced LAPC4 cells (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D). Interpretation of these results need to take into consideration the absence of miR-34a expression that was observed in the tumors from miR-34a transduced LAPC4 cells."
effects.notes: No inferential statistics reported for this comparison; abstract: 'we did not observe changes in tumor growth or CD44 expression; however, unexpectedly miR-34a expression was lost in vivo.' Because miR-34a was absent in the tumors (failed manipulation), a coder could reasonably code inconclusive. Type: different cell line (LAPC4 vs DU145) and lentiviral vs retroviral vector; authors say 'conceptually similar', so conceptual is a plausible alternative; coded close extension since the paradigm (miR-34a-transduced xenograft, CD44 Western) is recognizably the same.

effects.contrast: miR-34a oligos vs control oligos, with wild-type vs double-mutant (M1M2) CD44 3'UTR reporter
effects.timepoint: not applicable: single assay 48 h post-transfection
effects.description: miR-34a directly represses CD44 through binding sites in its 3'UTR: miR-34a decreases CD44 3'UTR luciferase reporter activity, and this repression is partially abrogated by mutating the binding sites.
effects.citation_sentence: This is similar to what was reported in Figure 4D of Liu et al. (2011) and described in Protocol 7 in the Registered Report (Li et al., 2015).
effects.evidence: Results, 'Evaluation of putative miR-34a binding sites' / Figure 3A: wild-type reporter miR-34a 0.99 vs control 1.00, "z = 0.517, uncorrected p=0.632"; double mutant 1.19 vs 1.00. "To summarize, we found results that were not consistent in direction with the original study and not statistically significant."
effects.notes: Coded as one claim (direct targeting of the CD44 3'UTR) covering the wild-type repression and the double-mutant abrogation comparisons; a coder could split into two rows (repression of WT reporter; abrogation by mutation), both of which would be failure. The paper's meta-analysis treats three comparisons separately (Figure 4B,C). Replication tested only the double mutant (original also single mutants). Same plasmids, cell line and design: direct.
